samples.summary: Data-model semantics change (a `list-item` now carries `headingLevel`) is not recorded in any design doc
samples.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61 — “**Architecture / data-model changes** belong in `docs/design/<area>/<topic>.md` … Update the existing doc when evolving an area”. This PR redefines an invariant of the `Block` model (previously `headingLevel` implied `type === 'heading'`; now a `list-item` legally carries an inert level that survives round-trip through the Yorkie tree attrs and the backend `docs-tree` serializer). The only prose is a TSDoc comment on `Block.headingLevel` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:54-61) and a task todo/lessons pair under docs/tasks/active/. `docs/design/docs/docs.md` is the canonical block-model doc (‘Design decisions → Block type’, line 113-116; ‘Empty list-item Backspace exits the list’, line 135-146) and is untouched, so the doc now describes a model rule the code no longer holds. If the maintainers treat #783 as a plain bug fix, CONTRIBUTING.md:11-12 lets it skip a design doc — hence medium confidence, not high.

samples.summary: Only `toggleList` exits through `unlistedBlockType`; the other two list-exit gestures still hardcode `'paragraph'`, so the same user intent gives two different results
samples.evidence: `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:297-301, Enter on an empty list item — “exit list by converting to paragraph”) and `Doc.deleteBackward` (document.ts:262-266, Backspace at offset 0 of an empty list item — documented in docs/design/docs/docs.md:135-146) both call `this.setBlockType(id, 'paragraph')` unchanged. Those are ‘remove the list’ paths just like the toolbar toggle, so a bulleted Heading 2 emptied and Enter/Backspace-ed out of the list still silently becomes body text — the exact failure #783 describes, via a different gesture. The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:46-52) lists ‘splitting a bulleted heading (Enter)’ as a non-goal, but that non-goal is about the *new* item after a mid-text split, not about the empty-item list-exit branch, so the gap looks unintended and undermines the stated point of the shared helper (‘keeps the three toggleList implementations from drifting’).

samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` does not constrain its input to a list item, so its contract is looser than its name and doc
samples.evidence: The helper returns `{type:'heading'}` for *any* block that has a `headingLevel`, including a block that is already a `heading`. All three current callers guard on `block.type === 'list-item'`, so behaviour is fine today, but as the model-layer helper documenting the retention rule it would be more self-enforcing to early-return for non-list-item blocks (or take the level rather than the block).

samples.summary: The invariant that makes the retained level safe lives only in a comment, not in a type or a check
samples.evidence: The TSDoc asserts “every reader (export, `blockStyleId`, toolbar labels) gates on `type === 'heading'`”. I verified that holds today (docx-exporter.ts:184, pdf-exporter.ts:201-205, named-styles.ts:106-109, text-style-options.ts:112/127, layout.ts:387), but nothing in the type system or a test prevents a future unguarded reader (e.g. `EditorAPI.getBlockType()` at editor.ts:2791-2795 already surfaces the level to callers regardless of type). A narrower representation, or a shared `getHeadingLevel(block)` accessor that applies the gate once, would carry the invariant instead of relying on every future reader remembering it.
searchedFor: grep headingLevel across packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src

finding.summary: Data-model semantics change (a `list-item` now carries `headingLevel`) is not recorded in any design doc
finding.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61 — “**Architecture / data-model changes** belong in `docs/design/<area>/<topic>.md` … Update the existing doc when evolving an area”. This PR redefines an invariant of the `Block` model (previously `headingLevel` implied `type === 'heading'`; now a `list-item` legally carries an inert level that survives round-trip through the Yorkie tree attrs and the backend `docs-tree` serializer). The only prose is a TSDoc comment on `Block.headingLevel` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:54-61) and a task todo/lessons pair under docs/tasks/active/. `docs/design/docs/docs.md` is the canonical block-model doc (‘Design decisions → Block type’, line 113-116; ‘Empty list-item Backspace exits the list’, line 135-146) and is untouched, so the doc now describes a model rule the code no longer holds. If the maintainers treat #783 as a plain bug fix, CONTRIBUTING.md:11-12 lets it skip a design doc — hence medium confidence, not high.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. Grepping `headingLevel` across ALL of docs/design (not just docs/design/docs) yields exactly one hit — docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md:69, a pre-existing style-mapping table unaffected by this change. Grepping `list-item` across docs/design yields 7 files (docs.md:115, docs-tables.md, docs-docx-import-export.md:255, docs-header-footer.md:79, docs-named-styles.md:66, docs-collaboration.md, cli.md), none of which mentions a list-item retaining a heading level. Grepping unlist/un-list/bullet/toggleList/unlistedBlockType/retain/preserv across docs/design surfaces only docs-font-controls.md:235,271-272, which concerns clear-formatting preserving block styles on a heading — a different rule. Repo-wide, `unlistedBlockType` appears only in source, tests, .agent-review artifacts, and docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md — never in a design doc. I also enumerated all 112 files under docs/design/** for a folded or renamed doc and found none. CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61 is quoted accurately. Two honest caveats keep my confidence low rather than high: (1) docs/design/docs/docs.md never actually asserts the old invariant (grepping `heading` in that file returns only lines 50 and 115), so the doc is silent rather than contradicted, weakening the reviewer's framing; (2) CONTRIBUTING.md:11-12 gives bug fixes a doc-free path and this change adds no field and no new CRDT attribute name, so whether a design doc was REQUIRED is genuinely arguable. Neither caveat is a named refutation ground, so the finding stays.

finding.summary: Only `toggleList` exits through `unlistedBlockType`; the other two list-exit gestures still hardcode `'paragraph'`, so the same user intent gives two different results
finding.evidence: `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:297-301, Enter on an empty list item — “exit list by converting to paragraph”) and `Doc.deleteBackward` (document.ts:262-266, Backspace at offset 0 of an empty list item — documented in docs/design/docs/docs.md:135-146) both call `this.setBlockType(id, 'paragraph')` unchanged. Those are ‘remove the list’ paths just like the toolbar toggle, so a bulleted Heading 2 emptied and Enter/Backspace-ed out of the list still silently becomes body text — the exact failure #783 describes, via a different gesture. The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:46-52) lists ‘splitting a bulleted heading (Enter)’ as a non-goal, but that non-goal is about the *new* item after a mid-text split, not about the empty-item list-exit branch, so the gap looks unintended and undermines the stated point of the shared helper (‘keeps the three toggleList implementations from drifting’).

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. `Doc.deleteBackward` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:262-266) and `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:297-301) both hardcode `this.setBlockType(id, 'paragraph')` for the empty-list-item exit, while `unlistedBlockType` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:337-344) is called only from the three toolbar `toggleList` sites (view/editor.ts:2870, view/text-editor.ts:2169, view/text-box-editor.ts:1125). Since the change makes a `list-item` retain `headingLevel`, both gestures are reachable for a bulleted heading and silently drop the level, so the same "remove the list" intent yields two different results. No guard makes these branches unreachable. The todo's Non-goals (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:46-52) exclude only the *new item* produced by a mid-text Enter split, not the empty-item list-exit branch — and docs/design/docs/docs.md:135-146 explicitly describes Backspace-on-empty as mirroring Enter's list exit, i.e. the repo treats these as the same gesture class as the toggle. Design-fit lane (spec conformance to #783's outcome plus the shared-helper reuse the change itself claims); major by kind, not refutable on any named ground.
